## The Core Claim

Contrary to Garrett Hardin's 'tragedy of the commons' prediction that shared resources are inevitably overexploited absent private property or top-down state control, empirical field studies of real irrigation systems, fisheries, and forests found that local communities repeatedly self-organize durable governance institutions -- monitoring, graduated sanctions, low-cost conflict resolution -- that sustainably manage common-pool resources without either privatization or centralized regulation. Elinor Ostrom won the 2009 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for this analysis of economic governance, especially the commons.
